title: Elder Sign - Scary Dice and Creepy Monsters
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CEF9v_JMVe8

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens the channel's horror-themed October 2022 with Elder Sign, Fantasy Flight's dice-game distillation of Arkham Horror and Eldritch Horror — a game he admits he should play more, since he enjoys it every time. He pitches it to newcomers: investigators with sanity and stamina, an Ancient One with a doom track, and six museum adventure cards, each a Yahtzee-style run of tasks (a skull, a terror symbol, seven clues) cleared in one turn or you take the bad stuff. The theme is thinner than its big-box cousins — emergent narrative traded for puzzle — so items, spells and allies matter chiefly as dice manipulation: locking, changing faces, adding the yellow and red dice.

Then the expansions. Grave Consequences, a print-on-demand pack, is the must-buy: an epic-battle variant that fixes the anaemic final fight, epitaph cards that give investigator deaths a story and a payoff, and phobia cards for when sanity hits zero. Gates of Arkham is his favourite way to play — it swaps the museum for Arkham locations (Ma's Boarding House, the Silver Twilight Lodge), adds factions, events, skills and gates to other worlds, and restores the theme without adding time. Omens of Ice and Omens of the Pharaoh are two-stage narrative expeditions with supply and storm tracks.

His recommended set: base game plus Gates of Arkham plus Grave Consequences, about an hour solo. He also recommends The Starry Wisdom Library, an anthology of invented occult books catalogued for a fictional 1877 auction.

----

Elder Sign strips theme for puzzle, then buys it back through expansions. When does a distilled version of a big game beat the original for you?
